name: correctly describes early-return gating vs misstates early-return as ensuring non-null
side_a: no_deduct if the answer explains that the early return prevents later code from running when drawer is null (i.e., later code only runs when drawer is non-null) and/or clearly distinguishes which parts depend on drawer versus those that don't.
side_b: deduct if the answer claims the method 'ensures' drawer is non-null by returning early or otherwise mischaracterizes the effect of the early return.

name: Recognizes in-method null-guard dependency vs claims external precondition/no direct dependency
side_a: no_deduct: Credit answers that explicitly ground the dependency in the method's own control flow (e.g., citing the early-return null check and/or subsequent calls on drawer), showing that the end-of-method code executes only when drawer is non-null.
side_b: deduct: Deduct when the answer denies a direct dependency and frames non-null as an external assumption/precondition (e.g., says the method assumes drawer is initialized before being called), thereby moving the dependency outside the method.
